checked_claims.note: The stable-graph genus and half-edge identities give sum_v(2g_v-2+n_v)=2g-2+n.
The reachable set is closed under one-edge vertex types, dimension drops by one, and its only RED-0001 pairs are (5,8) at depth zero and (3,12) at depth two.

Exact duality of finite-dimensional rational mixed Hodge structures turns THM-0003 at homological degree 16 into the asserted left-exact cohomology sequence. No Gysin degree shift or Tate twist belongs in this linear-dual formulation.

For a finite graph-automorphism group over Q, quotient-stack cohomology is computed by invariants; invariants and coinvariants are exact and dual as required. Taking a character-twisted invariant subspace of Q(-8) copies cannot introduce another Hodge type.
For the stated nonexceptional pairs, FND-0001 and THM-0005 give K=(W_jH^j(d))^vee with j=2d-16, hence Q(j/2-d)=Q(-8); odd j gives zero.
ATT-0142 types K(5,8). At (3,12), d=18 and j=20=vcd; the inclusive n-1=11=c(3) case of FND-0195 gives W_20H^20=Q(-10) copies, so (Q(-10)(18))^vee=Q(-8) copies.

THM-0006 and THM-0007 identify the relevant compact even cohomology with tautological cycle classes. Their degree-16 classes are algebraic of type (8,8), and purity gives actual copies of Q(-8); no converse from pure Tate to algebraic generation is used.
If i+j=16 are both odd, min(i,j)<=7. The published odd-cohomology vanishing range through degree 9 therefore kills one factor in every such Kunneth summand.

Induction on dimension covers every stable pair in the reachable set. Even Kunneth slots below 16 use THM-0002, endpoint slots use induction, odd-odd slots vanish, and the depth-two exceptional pair (3,12) is explicitly handled. No stable pair needed by the induction is omitted.

The quotient H^16/K embeds into a boundary group consisting only of Q(-8) copies. Polarizable pure weight-16 rational Hodge structures are semisimple, so the resulting extension splits as an actual Hodge-structure isomorphism, not merely after semisimplification. On the smooth proper 20-dimensional stack, Poincare duality gives H_16=Q(8) copies and H^24=Q(-12) copies with the stated twists.
The proof is expressly limited to the compact (5,8) lemma and makes no boundary-image or global campaign conclusion.

strongest_attack: The strongest attack is the hidden depth-two residual (3,12): the nonseparating divisor [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2] has a further nonseparating boundary Mbar_{3,12}, so immediate one-edge exclusion from RED-0001 is insufficient. This is load-bearing because (3,12) lies exactly at j=2d-16=vcd=20 and n-1=c(3)=11, with only endpoint-level slack in the peel argument. The attack does not succeed. FND-0195 includes this equality case, its exclusions are not engaged, and the peel uses the closed universal curve, Harer vanishing, Morita disposal, the vcd vanishing of M_{3,11}, and the Q(-9) psi-source with the correct Q(-1) shift. Thus K(3,12)=(Q(-10)(18))^vee=Q(-8). The remaining stack-versus-coarse, rational invariants-versus-coinvariants, degree and twist, Kunneth parity, determinant-character, and semisimplicity checks also close without leaving a surviving non-Tate summand.
theorem_statement: Using a verified C58-OPEN residual and a verified C58-BOUNDARY accounting, apply the boundary right-exact sequence of THM-0003 to conclude that H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8). A disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this compact group. This theorem does not conclude the campaign boundary-image theorem.
